To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alternative markets host 1) a large amount of ad-aggressive and 2) malicious applications, and that 3) some markets even allow malicious apps to be published and remain available.

(1) alternative application markets host a large amount of malware (e.g., 1.6% of the apps in one market), (2) alternative markets allow authors to publish malicious applications (e.g., in one market we found 1,200 malicious apps), and (3) alternative markets host a significant amount of ad-aggressive applications (e.g. 1% of the apps are ad-aggressive in one market).
• We crawled 8 Android alternative markets between June and Nov 2013.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) How many alternative application markets exist?
the problem of fast discovery of applications that are distributed in alternative Android markets.

(i) the discovery of Android applications in alternative markets; (ii) the detection of malware in alternative markets; and (iii) the analysis of the security policies enforced by alternative markets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current state of Android alternative markets is a mess.
alternative markets have the same risks as official markets, but are less regulated, and therefore pose a larger threat to users.
Android markets are not safe.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Android ecosystem is still far from being a malware-free environment, and that the problem is exacerbated by the existence of alternative markets.
Android alternative markets are an untapped resource for malware researchers.
alternative markets are not a safe haven for malware.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of alternative markets poses a significant challenge to the Android ecosystem, as they provide a fertile ground for malware authors to evade detection.
a single marketplace is not sufficient to detect all malicious Android apps.
the current approach of tracking Android malware in a single market is insufficient.
